topIssues.title: Vulnerable Kona accepts an invalid interop activation-block transition that canonical OP verification rejects.
topIssues.author: x15-eth
topIssues.body:
> A Kona interop verifier accepts an executing cross-chain message in the executing chain’s first interop block, while canonical OP verification rejects that transition. This creates a consensus/fault-proof validation split where Kona-based actors may compute or defend a different post-state/output root than canonical op-program / supervisor-derived validation.


`op-supernode` has its own executing-message verifier, and it does not apply the activation-block guard used by the canonical interop/proof path.

[https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/be742e31ae58ee21dd4431cff839a07c63845570/op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/algo.go#L140-L144](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/be742e31ae58ee21dd4431cff839a07c63845570/op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/algo.go#L140-L144)

[https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/be742e31ae58ee21dd4431cff839a07c63845570/op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/algo.go#L170-L211](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/be742e31ae58ee21dd4431cff839a07c63845570/op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/algo.go#L170-L211)

Canonical logic rejects interop messages when either side lands in the interop activation block. In that case, `op-program` treats the block as invalid and replaces it with a deposits-only block, which removes the invalid state transition.

[https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/be742e31ae58ee21dd4431cff839a07c63845570/op-supervisor/supervisor/backend/depset/links.go#L43-L55](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/be742e31ae58ee21dd4431cff839a07c63845570/op-supervisor/supervisor/backend/depset/links.go#L43-L55)

[https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/be742e31ae58ee21dd4431cff839a07c63845570/op-supervisor/supervisor/backend/depset/links.go#L43-L55](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/be742e31ae58ee21dd4431cff839a07c63845570/op-supervisor/supervisor/backend/depset/links.go#L43-L55)

[https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/be742e31ae58ee21dd4431cff839a07c63845570/op-supervisor/supervisor/backend/depset/links.go#L43-L55](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/be742e31ae58ee21dd4431cff839a07c63845570/op-supervisor/supervisor/backend/depset/links.go#L43-L55)

The vulnerable path accepts the activation-boundary executing message, so it can keep the original optimistic output root, including a `L2ToL1MessagePasser` storage root that contains a withdrawal which canonical execution would not accept.

[https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/be742e31ae58ee21dd4431cff839a07c63845570/op-supervisor/supervisor/backend/depset/links.go#L43-L55](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/be742e31ae58ee21dd4431cff839a07c63845570/op-supervisor/supervisor/backend/depset/links.go#L43-L55)

[https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/be742e31ae58ee21dd4431cff839a07c63845570/op-supervisor/supervisor/backend/depset/links.go#L43-L55](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/be742e31ae58ee21dd4431cff839a07c63845570/op-supervisor/supervisor/backend/depset/links.go#L43-L55)

## Impact
The concrete impact is fault-proof / interop verification divergence

A vulnerable Kona verifier accepts an executing cross-chain message in the executing chain’s interop activation block. The canonical Go path rejects that same block because executing messages are forbidden in the first interop block.

So two proof/verification paths can disagree on the same transition:

- Vulnerable Kona: treats the activation-block executing message as valid.
- Canonical op-program / op-supervisor behavior: treats it as invalid and replaces/removes that bad block from the valid output path.
Concrete consequences:

1. Divergent post-state at a dispute boundary A Kona-based prover/challenger may compute a different output root than canonical op-program.

2. Incorrect dispute behavior for Kona-based actors A proposer, challenger, or monitor relying on vulnerable Kona could defend or fail to challenge the wrong output. This can cause operational failure or bond loss, but proposer/challenger bonds are excluded from the Critical funds-loss impact you care about.

3. Potential invalid-output risk only if another path accepts the bad root The serious impact would be bad output root gets proposed, survives dispute, and finalizes a withdrawal.

## Recommendation
Add the same activation-block guard to op-supernode executing-message verification that canonical interop validation uses.

Specifically:

- Reject executing messages when the executing chain timestamp is the interop activation block.
- Reject messages whose initiating timestamp is the source chain’s interop activation block.
- Add regression tests for both initiating-side and executing-side activation boundaries.
- Require challenger/monitor configurations to include a canonical proof-program-backed view or otherwise detect divergence from supernode-derived roots.
- Treat supernode-only agreement as insufficient for dispute safety at fork activation boundaries.

## POC
Below is the full repro diff. It adds two PoC tests:

- Go PoC: proves canonical op-program rejects the unreplaced activation-boundary claim when it carries a withdrawal-bearing output.
- Solidity PoC: proves that if that withdrawal-bearing output is accepted into a resolved superroot game, OptimismPortal2 can finalize the withdrawal.

```bash
go test ./op-program/client/interop \
  -run TestPoCActivationBoundaryExecutingMessageWithWithdrawalBearingOutputIsRejectedByProgram \
  -count=1 -v
```

```bash
DEV_FEATURE__OPTIMISM_PORTAL_INTEROP=true forge test --deny never \
  --match-path test/poc/SuperRootActivationWithdrawalPoC.t.sol \
  --match-test test_poc_activationBoundaryWithdrawalFinalizesThroughResolvedSuperRoot -vv
```

Both passed.

```diff
diff --git a/op-program/client/interop/activation_withdrawal_poc_test.go b/op-program/client/interop/activation_withdrawal_poc_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..a1f73fd242
--- /dev/null
+++ b/op-program/client/interop/activation_withdrawal_poc_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,141 @@
+package interop
+
+import (
+	"errors"
+	"math/rand"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-program/client/boot"
+	"github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-program/client/claim"
+	interopTypes "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-program/client/interop/types"
+	test2 "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-program/client/l1/test"
+	"github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-program/client/l2/test"
+	"github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-service/eth"
+	"github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-service/testlog"
+	"github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-service/testutils"
+	supervisortypes "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-supervisor/supervisor/types"
+	"github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/common"
+	gethTypes "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/core/types"
+	"github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/log"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+func TestPoCActivationBoundaryExecutingMessageWithWithdrawalBearingOutputIsRejectedByProgram(t *testing.T) {
+	logger := testlog.Logger(t, log.LevelError)
+	configSource, agreedSuperRoot, tasksStub := setupTwoChains()
+	defer tasksStub.AssertExpectations(t)
+
+	rng := rand.New(rand.NewSource(470272))
+	configA := configSource.rollupCfgs[0]
+	configB := configSource.rollupCfgs[1]
+	chainIDA := eth.ChainIDFromBig(configA.L2ChainID)
+	chainIDB := eth.ChainIDFromBig(configB.L2ChainID)
+
+	activation := uint64(2) * configA.BlockTime
+	for _, cfg := range configSource.rollupCfgs {
+		cfg.InteropTime = &activation
+	}
+
+	initLog := &gethTypes.Log{
+		Address: initiatingMessageOrigin,
+		Topics:  []common.Hash{initiatingMessageTopic},
+	}
+	exec := supervisortypes.Message{
+		Identifier: supervisortypes.Identifier{
+			Origin:      initiatingMessageOrigin,
+			BlockNumber: 2,
+			LogIndex:    0,
+			Timestamp:   activation,
+			ChainID:     chainIDA,
+		},
+		PayloadHash: initPayloadHash,
+	}
+
+	block1A, _ := createBlock(rng, configA, 1, nil)
+	block1B, _ := createBlock(rng, configB, 1, nil)
+	block2A, block2AReceipts := createBlock(rng, configA, 2, gethTypes.Receipts{{Logs: []*gethTypes.Log{initLog}}})
+	block2B, block2BReceipts := createBlock(rng, configB, 2, gethTypes.Receipts{{
+		Logs: []*gethTypes.Log{convertExecutingMessageToLog(t, exec)},
+	}})
+
+	pendingA := createOutput(block2A.Hash())
+	pendingB := createOutput(block2B.Hash())
+	pendingB.MessagePasserStorageRoot = eth.Bytes32(common.HexToHash(
+		"0x47027200000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000aa",
+	))
+	badWithdrawalBearingOutput := eth.OutputRoot(pendingB)
+
+	finalTransitionState := &interopTypes.TransitionState{
+		SuperRoot: agreedSuperRoot.Marshal(),
+		PendingProgress: []interopTypes.OptimisticBlock{
+			{BlockHash: block2A.Hash(), OutputRoot: eth.OutputRoot(pendingA)},
+			{BlockHash: block2B.Hash(), OutputRoot: badWithdrawalBearingOutput},
+		},
+		Step: ConsolidateStep,
+	}
+	agreedPrestate := finalTransitionState.Hash()
+
+	l2PreimageOracle, _ := test.NewStubOracle(t)
+	l2PreimageOracle.TransitionStates[agreedPrestate] = finalTransitionState
+	l2PreimageOracle.Outputs[common.Hash(agreedSuperRoot.Chains[0].Output)] = createOutput(block1A.Hash())
+	l2PreimageOracle.Outputs[common.Hash(agreedSuperRoot.Chains[1].Output)] = createOutput(block1B.Hash())
+	l2PreimageOracle.Outputs[common.Hash(eth.OutputRoot(pendingA))] = pendingA
+	l2PreimageOracle.Outputs[common.Hash(badWithdrawalBearingOutput)] = pendingB
+	l2PreimageOracle.Blocks[block1A.Hash()] = block1A
+	l2PreimageOracle.Blocks[block1B.Hash()] = block1B
+	l2PreimageOracle.Blocks[block2A.Hash()] = block2A
+	l2PreimageOracle.Blocks[block2B.Hash()] = block2B
+	l2PreimageOracle.Receipts[block2A.Hash()] = block2AReceipts
+	l2PreimageOracle.Receipts[block2B.Hash()] = block2BReceipts
+
+	depositsOnlyBlock, depositsOnlyReceipts := createBlock(rng, configB, 2, nil)
+	depositsOnlyOutput := createOutput(depositsOnlyBlock.Hash())
+	depositsOnlyOutputRoot := eth.OutputRoot(depositsOnlyOutput)
+	require.NotEqual(t, badWithdrawalBearingOutput, depositsOnlyOutputRoot)
+	require.NotEqual(t, pendingB.MessagePasserStorageRoot, depositsOnlyOutput.MessagePasserStorageRoot)
+
+	tasksStub.ExpectBuildDepositOnlyBlock(
+		common.Hash{},
+		agreedSuperRoot.Chains[1].Output,
+		depositsOnlyBlock.Hash(),
+		depositsOnlyOutputRoot,
+	)
+	l2PreimageOracle.Blocks[depositsOnlyBlock.Hash()] = depositsOnlyBlock
+	l2PreimageOracle.Outputs[common.Hash(depositsOnlyOutputRoot)] = depositsOnlyOutput
+	l2PreimageOracle.Receipts[depositsOnlyBlock.Hash()] = depositsOnlyReceipts
+
+	badUnreplacedClaim := common.Hash(eth.SuperRoot(&eth.SuperV1{
+		Timestamp: agreedSuperRoot.Timestamp + 1,
+		Chains: []eth.ChainIDAndOutput{
+			{ChainID: chainIDA, Output: eth.OutputRoot(pendingA)},
+			{ChainID: chainIDB, Output: badWithdrawalBearingOutput},
+		},
+	}))
+	canonicalReplacedClaim := common.Hash(eth.SuperRoot(&eth.SuperV1{
+		Timestamp: agreedSuperRoot.Timestamp + 1,
+		Chains: []eth.ChainIDAndOutput{
+			{ChainID: chainIDA, Output: eth.OutputRoot(pendingA)},
+			{ChainID: chainIDB, Output: depositsOnlyOutputRoot},
+		},
+	}))
+	require.NotEqual(t, badUnreplacedClaim, canonicalReplacedClaim)
+
+	l1Oracle := test2.NewStubOracle(t)
+	for _, chainID := range configSource.chainIDs {
+		rollupCfg, err := configSource.RollupConfig(chainID)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		l1Oracle.Blocks[rollupCfg.Genesis.L1.Hash] = &testutils.MockBlockInfo{
+			InfoHash: rollupCfg.Genesis.L1.Hash,
+			InfoNum:  rollupCfg.Genesis.L1.Number,
+			InfoTime: rollupCfg.Genesis.L2Time,
+		}
+	}
+
+	err := runInteropProgram(logger, &boot.BootInfoInterop{
+		AgreedPrestate: agreedPrestate,
+		GameTimestamp:  agreedSuperRoot.Timestamp + 100000,
+		Claim:          badUnreplacedClaim,
+		Configs:        configSource,
+	}, l1Oracle, l2PreimageOracle, tasksStub)
+	require.True(t, errors.Is(err, claim.ErrClaimNotValid), "canonical interop program should reject the withdrawal-bearing activation-boundary claim, got %v", err)
+}
diff --git a/packages/contracts-bedrock/test/poc/SuperRootActivationWithdrawalPoC.t.sol b/packages/contracts-bedrock/test/poc/SuperRootActivationWithdrawalPoC.t.sol
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..6b445a62bf
--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/contracts-bedrock/test/poc/SuperRootActivationWithdrawalPoC.t.sol
@@ -0,0 +1,113 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+pragma solidity 0.8.15;
+
+import { OptimismPortal2_TestInit } from "test/L1/OptimismPortal2.t.sol";
+import { DeployUtils } from "scripts/libraries/DeployUtils.sol";
+import { Types } from "src/libraries/Types.sol";
+import { Hashing } from "src/libraries/Hashing.sol";
+import { GameTypes, Claim, GameStatus } from "src/dispute/lib/Types.sol";
+import { IOptimismPortal2 as IOptimismPortal } from "interfaces/L1/IOptimismPortal2.sol";
+import { IDisputeGame } from "interfaces/dispute/IDisputeGame.sol";
+import { ISuperFaultDisputeGame } from "interfaces/dispute/ISuperFaultDisputeGame.sol";
+
+contract SuperRootActivationWithdrawalPoC_Test is OptimismPortal2_TestInit {
+    bytes32 internal constant EMPTY_STORAGE_ROOT = 0x56e81f171bcc55a6ff8345e692c0f86e5b48e01b996cadc001622fb5e363b421;
+
+    function setUp() public override {
+        super.setUp();
+        _installSuperCannonKonaGameImpl();
+    }
+
+    function test_poc_activationBoundaryWithdrawalFinalizesThroughResolvedSuperRoot() external {
+        uint256 activationTimestamp = _proposedBlockNumber + 470_272;
+
+        Types.OutputRootProof memory canonicalNoWithdrawalProof = _outputRootProof;
+        canonicalNoWithdrawalProof.messagePasserStorageRoot = EMPTY_STORAGE_ROOT;
+        bytes32 canonicalNoWithdrawalOutputRoot = Hashing.hashOutputRootProof(canonicalNoWithdrawalProof);
+
+        require(_outputRoot == Hashing.hashOutputRootProof(_outputRootProof), "bad fixture output root");
+        require(canonicalNoWithdrawalOutputRoot != _outputRoot, "canonical and withdrawal roots unexpectedly match");
+
+        IDisputeGame canonicalGame =
+            _createDisputeGame(GameTypes.SUPER_CANNON_KONA, canonicalNoWithdrawalOutputRoot, activationTimestamp);
+        uint256 canonicalGameIndex = disputeGameFactory.gameCount() - 1;
+        vm.warp(block.timestamp + 1 seconds);
+        vm.expectRevert(IOptimismPortal.OptimismPortal_InvalidOutputRootProof.selector);
+        optimismPortal2.proveWithdrawalTransaction({
+            _tx: _defaultTx,
+            _disputeGameIndex: canonicalGameIndex,
+            _outputRootProof: _outputRootProof,
+            _withdrawalProof: _withdrawalProof
+        });
+        require(address(canonicalGame) != address(0), "canonical game unused");
+
+        ISuperFaultDisputeGame vulnerableGame = ISuperFaultDisputeGame(
+            payable(address(_createDisputeGame(GameTypes.SUPER_CANNON_KONA, _outputRoot, activationTimestamp + 1)))
+        );
+        uint256 vulnerableGameIndex = disputeGameFactory.gameCount() - 1;
+
+        Claim perChainRoot = vulnerableGame.rootClaimByChainId(systemConfig.l2ChainId());
+        assertEq(perChainRoot.raw(), _outputRoot);
+        assertEq(
+            vulnerableGame.rootClaim().raw(),
+            Hashing.hashSuperRootProof(_singleChainSuperRoot(_outputRoot, activationTimestamp + 1))
+        );
+        assertTrue(vulnerableGame.wasRespectedGameTypeWhenCreated());
+
+        vm.warp(block.timestamp + vulnerableGame.maxClockDuration().raw() + 1 seconds);
+
+        vm.expectEmit(address(optimismPortal2));
+        emit WithdrawalProven(_withdrawalHash, alice, bob);
+        vm.expectEmit(address(optimismPortal2));
+        emit WithdrawalProvenExtension1(_withdrawalHash, address(this));
+        optimismPortal2.proveWithdrawalTransaction({
+            _tx: _defaultTx,
+            _disputeGameIndex: vulnerableGameIndex,
+            _outputRootProof: _outputRootProof,
+            _withdrawalProof: _withdrawalProof
+        });
+
+        vulnerableGame.resolveClaim(0, 0);
+        assertEq(uint8(vulnerableGame.resolve()), uint8(GameStatus.DEFENDER_WINS));
+
+        uint256 bobBalanceBefore = bob.balance;
+        vm.warp(block.timestamp + optimismPortal2.proofMaturityDelaySeconds() + 1 seconds);
+
+        vm.expectEmit(true, true, false, true);
+        emit WithdrawalFinalized(_withdrawalHash, true);
+        optimismPortal2.finalizeWithdrawalTransaction(_defaultTx);
+
+        assertEq(bob.balance, bobBalanceBefore + _defaultTx.value);
+        assertTrue(optimismPortal2.finalizedWithdrawals(_withdrawalHash));
+    }
+
+    function _installSuperCannonKonaGameImpl() internal {
+        bytes memory immutableArgs;
+        (immutableArgs,,) = getSuperFaultDisputeGameImmutableArgs(Claim.wrap(bytes32(uint256(0x470272))));
+
+        address gameImpl = DeployUtils.create1({
+            _name: "SuperFaultDisputeGame",
+            _args: DeployUtils.encodeConstructor(
+                abi.encodeCall(ISuperFaultDisputeGame.__constructor__, (_getSuperGameConstructorParams()))
+            )
+        });
+
+        _setGame(gameImpl, GameTypes.SUPER_CANNON_KONA, immutableArgs);
+
+        vm.prank(superchainConfig.guardian());
+        anchorStateRegistry.setRespectedGameType(GameTypes.SUPER_CANNON_KONA);
+    }
+
+    function _singleChainSuperRoot(
+        bytes32 outputRoot,
+        uint256 timestamp
+    )
+        internal
+        view
+        returns (Types.SuperRootProof memory proof_)
+    {
+        Types.OutputRootWithChainId[] memory roots = new Types.OutputRootWithChainId[](1);
+        roots[0] = Types.OutputRootWithChainId({ chainId: systemConfig.l2ChainId(), root: outputRoot });
+        proof_ = Types.SuperRootProof({ version: bytes1(uint8(1)), timestamp: uint64(timestamp), outputRoots: roots });
+    }
+}
```

What this demonstrates: the canonical proof path would replace the activation-boundary block and reject the bad superroot, but the bridge contracts themselves will finalize a withdrawal once that withdrawal-bearing per-chain output root is embedded in a respected, defender-won superroot dispute game.

**Description**
After the Karst upgrade is deployed to all networks, the Karst-specific upgrade transactions in `GenerateNUTBundle.s.sol` should be removed as they're only needed for that upgrade.

**Transactions to Remove**

In `_preImplementationDeployments()` (lines 169-172):
- ConditionalDeployer implementation deployment
- ConditionalDeployer proxy upgrade

In `_preL2CMDeployment()` (lines 184-187):
- L2ProxyAdmin upgrade transaction

The Karst conditional checks and associated helper functions (`_generateConditionalDeployerTxns`, `_generateL2ProxyAdminUpgrade`) can be removed once all chains have completed the Karst upgrade.

topPRs.title: feat(rust): add derivation pipeline test framework
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Add `rust/derivation-tests` crate — a framework for AI agents to construct deterministic L1+L2 chains and test the OP Stack derivation pipeline
- Provides L1/L2 chain builders, batch encoding (singular batches, zlib/brotli compression, channel framing), in-memory EVM state with trie root computation, and JSON-RPC + beacon API servers
- Targets testing across op-program, kona-proofs, op-node, and kona-node using the same synthetic chain data

### Modules

| Module | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `config` | Deterministic rollup configuration with all hardforks active from genesis |
| `state` | In-memory EVM state DB (revm CacheDB) with Merkle trie root computation and EIP-1186 proofs |
| `l1` / `l2` | Chain builders for constructing valid block sequences with proper parent hashing |
| `batch` | Channel encoding: singular batches → compress → frame → calldata |
| `server` | jsonrpsee L1/L2 RPC servers + axum beacon blob API on random ports |
| `harness` | High-level `DerivationTest` entry point, runner stubs for op-program/kona |
| `roots` | Output root (V0) and super root (V1) computation via kona-protocol |

## Test plan

- [x] 10 unit tests pass (config determinism, state roots, batch encoding roundtrip, channel framing)
- [x] 5 integration tests pass (empty blocks, batch submission, multi-block L2, L1 chain structure)
- [x] 1 ignored test stub for op-program invocation (requires external binary)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p derivation-tests -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] `cargo test -p derivation-tests` — 16 pass, 0 fail

topPRs.title: feat(kona/derive): pure sync deriver with full span-batch overlap check (phase 3/6)
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of 6 — stacked on top of #20703 (Phase 2) → #20702 (Phase 1).

Builds a pure (sync, IO-free, `no_std`) `Deriver` on top of phase 2's
`crate::core::*` primitives, and closes the post-Holocene span-batch
overlap content-check spec gap that both op-node
(`op-node/rollup/derive/batch_stage.go:139`) and kona's async pipeline
(`crates/protocol/protocol/src/batch/span.rs:591`) skip today.

**Closes spec gap: full byte-wise post-Holocene span-batch overlap content check** — implemented in `pure/overlap.rs` and exercised by both unit and replay tests.

## Public API (`kona_derive::pure`)

- `Deriver::new(rollup_cfg, l1_cfg, sys_config, safe_head, dependency_set)`
- `Deriver::derive(safe_head) -> (Derivation, DeriveTrace)` — **never returns `Err`**
- `Deriver::add_l1_input(L1Input) -> Result<(), CriticalError>`
- `Deriver::add_span_batch_overlap(SpanBatchOverlap) -> Result<(), CriticalError>`
- `Deriver::reset(safe_head, sys_config) -> DeriveTrace`
- `extract_l1_input(header, txs, receipts, rollup_cfg) -> L1Input` — **filter-only, sysconfig-blind**

`Derivation` variants the caller matches exhaustively:
- `Attributes { attrs }` — emit and advance the engine.
- `NeedL1Input` — fetch + extract + `add_l1_input`.
- `NeedSpanBatchOverlap { parent, content }` — fetch L2 range + `add_span_batch_overlap`.

## Contract invariants

Encoded in the types and verified by tests:

- `derive` never errors. Malformed frames / channels / batches / deposit logs / config logs surface as typed `TraceEntry::*Dropped` / `*Failed` entries.
- `add_*` only error on contract violations (`NonContiguousL1Input`, `L1InputParentMismatch`, `UnsolicitedOverlap`, `OverlapParentMismatch`, `OverlapRangeMismatch`).
- No `tracing::*` calls inside `pure/`. Callers translate `DeriveTrace` entries.
- `extract_l1_input` does no fallible parsing; `L1Input` carries raw `Vec<Log>` and `Vec<(Address, Bytes)>`.
- `extract_l1_input` does **not** accept a `SystemConfig`; the dynamic `batcher_addr` filter lives in the deriver (sysconfig-blind helper).
- `SpanBatchOverlapBlock.txs: Vec<Bytes>` — raw RLP throughout, no encode/decode round-trip in the overlap check.
- `pure/` is `no_std`; verified by `--target=riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf`.
- Every `match` on `Derivation` and `TraceEntry` inside `pure/` is exhaustive; strict typed reason enums everywhere, no `String` reason fields.
- `reset(safe_head, sys_config)` clears pending channels, decoded-but-un-emitted batches, active overlap state, and the L1 input buffer; supplied `sys_config` becomes the new rolling sysconfig.

## Verification gates

All run from `rust/`:

- `cargo build -p kona-derive --no-default-features` — **PASS**
- `cargo build -p kona-derive --no-default-features --target=riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf` — **PASS** (no_std proof)
- `cargo build -p kona-derive` (default) — **PASS**
- `cargo test -p kona-derive --lib pure::` — **20/20 PASS** (both with and without default features)
- `cargo test -p kona-derive --test replay` — **3/3 PASS**
- `cargo clippy -p kona-derive --all-targets -- -D warnings` — **CLEAN**
- `cargo clippy -p kona-derive --no-default-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` — **CLEAN**

Full lib-test result: **250 passed, 1 failed**. The single failure is the pre-existing flake `test_span_batch_extraction_error_flushes_stage` (a `tracing` global-default subscriber collision that reproduces on the phase 2 baseline). Not introduced by this PR.

Downstream consumers (`kona-node-service`, `kona-proof`, `kona-driver`) compile cleanly against the new surface.

## Replay test — synthetic fixtures

The replay test at `crates/protocol/derive/tests/replay.rs` uses **synthetic** fixtures rather than recorded mainnet data. Recording a real mainnet fixture requires both an L1 RPC and a beacon-chain endpoint covering the chosen range plus an L2 lookup snapshot — not available in the environment this PR was assembled in.

The synthetic fixtures hit each load-bearing code path the plan calls out:

- `replay_hardfork_activation_boundary` — feeds an L1 stream straddling a Granite activation timestamp and asserts the deriver continues without any soft-reset signal. This closes the otherwise-hidden risk that the deleted `Signal::Activation` site (`actor.rs:130` in kona-node) was load-bearing — the hard gate the plan names before phase 4 can proceed.
- `replay_sysconfig_and_deposit_paths` — feeds a real `ConfigUpdate` log and a real `TransactionDeposited` log alongside malformed versions of each, and asserts the deriver emits exactly one `SystemConfigUpdated`, one `SystemConfigUpdateDropped`, and one `DepositLogDropped`.
- `replay_long_empty_sequence_stays_quiet` — sanity check: 40 empty L1 blocks produce no spurious drops.

`crates/protocol/derive/tests/fixtures/README.md` documents the synthetic-vs-real situation, what would be needed to record real fixtures, and how the future `record-fixtures` cargo feature will be wired so CI replays from frozen bytes only.

## Unit test coverage

Per-component tests asserting specific `TraceEntry` shapes (no log-grep):

- `pure::extract::tests` (4) — batch-inbox filter, deposit log filter, config log filter, failed-receipt skip.
- `pure::overlap::tests` (5) — accept-on-full-match, drop on tx-count mismatch / tx mismatch / l1-origin mismatch / missing L1 info tx.
- `pure::deriver::tests` (11) — empty path, non-contiguous L1 error, parent-mismatch error, unsolicited-overlap error, reset clears state + emits `Reset` event, malformed sysconfig log → `SystemConfigUpdateDropped`, malformed deposit log → `DepositLogDropped`, batcher-from mismatch → `BatchInboxTxIgnoredFromMismatch`, garbage calldata → `FramesParseFailed`, sequencing-window expiry → `EmptyBatchGenerated`, future-safe-head sanity.

Total: 20 unit + 3 replay = 23 new tests, all passing.

## Files

- `crates/protocol/derive/src/lib.rs` — wire up `pure::*`; hoist test macros out of `test_utils/` so `--no-default-features` lib tests can construct frames.
- `crates/protocol/derive/src/pure/` — new module: `deriver.rs`, `types.rs`, `extract.rs`, `overlap.rs`, `mod.rs`.
- `crates/protocol/derive/src/stages/traversal/{indexed,polling}.rs` — minor clippy fix (`const fn` for `update_origin`), unblocks `clippy -D warnings`.
- `crates/protocol/derive/src/test_macros.rs` — moved from `test_utils/macros.rs` so the `frame!` macro is available without `feature = "async"`.

topPRs.title: fix: align raft-wal LogsDB error behavior
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Align raftwallogdb error behavior with the OP supervisor legacy LogsDB contract. This keeps callers seeing the same sentinel errors and the same important message prefixes while the storage implementation moves to raft-wal.

One concrete filter-facing motivation is `LogsDBChainIngester.writeFetchedBlock`: it classifies `types.ErrConflict` from `processBlockLogs` as a database conflict state. Before this PR, raftwallogdb returned `ErrOutOfOrder` for some `SealBlock` application conflicts, such as wrong block number or timestamp regression. That would have bypassed the interop filter's conflict handling and surfaced as a generic ingest error instead of entering the database-conflict path.

Specifically, this updates:
- `FindSealedBlock`: future blocks use `block <n> is not known yet: future data`; blocks before the first retained block wrap `skipped data` with `failed to find sealed block <n>`
- `AddLog`: logs before any sealed parent, logs on genesis/zero parent, wrong parent, duplicate indexes, and skipped indexes all return `ErrOutOfOrder` under `failed to apply log`
- `SealBlock`: wrong block number, wrong parent hash, timestamp regression, and pending-log parent conflicts return `ErrConflict` under `failed to seal block`
- `Contains`: block 0 is always `ErrConflict`; future blocks preserve the timestamp-invariant split between `ErrFuture` and `ErrConflict`; timestamp mismatch, missing log index, and checksum mismatch return `ErrConflict` with legacy-style messages
- `OpenBlock`: block 0 and first-nonzero-anchor boundaries return the expected `ErrSkipped` behavior
- `Rewind`: empty DB rewinds return `ErrFuture`, rewinds before the first retained block still clear the DB, and hash mismatches remain `ErrConflict`

The tests add focused coverage for those parity cases, including the checksum/timestamp message forms and the empty-DB AddLog wording.

## Validation
- `go test ./op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/raftwallogdb`
- `go test ./op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop`
- `go test ./op-interop-filter/filter`

topPRs.title: refactor(kona/derive): carve sync cores into src/core/ (phase 2/6)
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Phase 2 of 6 — stacked on top of #20702 (Phase 1).

## What's happening

Lift the IO-free state-machine work out of `stages/channel/channel_assembler.rs`, `stages/batch/{batch_stream,batch_validator}.rs`, and `attributes/stateful.rs` into a new `src/core/{channel,batch,attributes}/` module, `pub(crate)` for now. The async stages refactor to delegate to `core::*`. Phase 3 will build `pure::Deriver` on top of the same primitives.

* **`core::channel`** — sync post-Holocene channel assembler: timeout check, frame ingestion (Holocene's single-channel rule + strict frame ordering via the existing `OrderedChannel` type), fork-aware max-RLP-bytes limit. `stages/channel/channel_assembler.rs` keeps its public field shape (so existing tests are unmodified) and forwards into `core::channel::{check_timeout, max_rlp_bytes_per_channel, process_frame}`. All `tracing::*` calls stay on the async wrapper.

* **`core::batch`** — sync span-batch hydration (drains a `SpanBatch` into a buffer of `SingleBatch`es) and sync empty-batch derivation for the sequence-window-expired path. `BatchStream::try_hydrate_buffer` and `BatchValidator::try_derive_empty_batch` delegate.

* **`core::attributes`** — sync payload-attribute composition: the block-mismatch reset check, deposit-log decoding (which was async-shaped but never awaited an actual IO call), upgrade-tx selection across all forks through Karst/Interop, L1 info tx encoding, gas-limit + EIP-1559 + Jovian min-base-fee composition. `attributes/stateful.rs` shrinks to its IO wrapper plus the `tracing::*` calls.

## Scope: Holocene only

Only the Holocene-active paths are carved out. Pre-Holocene paths in the same files (the legacy `BatchQueue` stage, the `ChannelBank` multi-channel assembler, etc.) stay in `stages/` until Phase 6b deletes them wholesale. This matches the plan's hard-scope boundary: pure derivation never supports pre-Holocene rules.

## Design rules honored

- `core/` is `pub(crate)`. Phase 6b promotes to `pub` as a stable seam for future extraction.
- No `tracing::*` calls inside `core/` — the async stages still emit the same log messages they did before, in the same order. The eventual pure deriver translates structured outcomes to traces in Phase 3.
- `core/` is `no_std`-clean — verified against the kona-client target (`riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf`), which is what the just `check-no-std` target covers.
- No behavior change. The carve-out is a structural refactor; existing stage tests pass unchanged.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|------|--------|
| `cargo build -p kona-derive --no-default-features` | passes |
| `cargo build -p kona-derive --no-default-features --target=riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf` | passes (kona's actual `no_std` target — the plan named `riscv64gc-unknown-none-elf` which kona doesn't use) |
| `cargo build -p kona-derive --all-targets` (default features) | passes |
| `cargo build --workspace` | passes |
| `cargo test -p kona-derive --lib -- --test-threads=1` | 230 pass, 1 pre-existing flake (`test_span_batch_extraction_error_flushes_stage` — calls `tracing_subscriber::Registry::default().with(layer).init()` which panics on duplicate global subscriber installs; same flake reported on baseline, not in scope) |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | passes |

New `core::*` unit tests (15) cover: channel assembly happy path + timeout detection + non-starting-frame drop + size-limit drop bedrock + size-limit drop fjord + malformed-frame keeps channel; span batch hydration single block; empty-batch EOF inside window + empty-batch generated first-of-epoch; attributes math single block + block-mismatch same-epoch + block-mismatch epoch-boundary + block-mismatch no-error + broken time invariant + ecotone activation tx count.

## Notable deviation from plan

The plan named `riscv64gc-unknown-none-elf` as the no_std verification target. kona-client and the workspace's `just check-no-std` use `riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf` (per `rust/justfile` and CHANGELOG #868). Used the actual one. `core/` is `no_std`-clean against it.

Fixes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20697
Part of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20695
